unresolved.message: @Brent Trotter I like how succinct this version is. The word "prioritize" is standing out to me and doesn't feel like it fits with the tone of the rest of the content. I think it's because it feels very productivity-oriented to me and reading these articles might be the most relaxing and fun thing I do online all day. :) Would "feature" work in its place? That might imply that there are stories outside of these topics that we're showing, but we're just not featuring them.

@Brent Trotter I lean towards this version more so than the others because it's clear that: me choosing topics = stuff I'll see in my feed/stuff is tailored to me

In the versions where it's a form of +"some other picks": I assume is also based on my interests but worry I may get stuff I don't want. So this version feels the most direct to me!

does the user understand we're taking this data and using it to recommend stories. 

should there be more substance around that here? and cover us for future states?
will it "just" be stories related to my interests; make clear it'll be other too
I prefer the simple + human variant. I also think machine-learning sounds jargon-y. (And maybe it won't come across as a perk to some users?)
Not sure "Tune" as a verb here gives enough signal. Feels like "fine-tune" is fine (ha) as a phrase, but tune seperated from it is a smidge harder to grok.
(Sorry my first comments around the return modal should apply here too) but I think this first time intro can be more exciting like "See more of the stories you love"
Do you need to mention the curators or ML at all? I think you could just keep the most vital info of how many topics to pick and "update anytime"

Riff: 
Fine-tune your feed

is nice and punchy
Who are the expert curators? Are they Firefox staff / members of the community? I wonder if it's worth getting more explicit about who the "our" is here.
I love the idea of calling out a timeframe ("today") because it could push folks to look at these more often if they're new.
Curious if legal is requiring us to disclose the ML here or not.
If you're trying to avoid "feed", you could frame it around "stories" like: "See the stories that interest you" "Pick your interests, see more stories you love"
I wonder if this might be something that appears underneath the topics. It feels more like "hint text" for an input field than lead-worthy.
